Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION NO. 39 S. 2mo 19 April 2010 HON. HAROUN ALRASHID LUCMAN, JR. Regional Secretary DILG - ARMM ARMM Complex, Cotabato City Dear Secretary Lucman: This has reference to His Honor's April 7, 2010 letter, inquiring from this Office the extent of the powers and authority conferred upon Hon. Guimid Matalam, Assistant Secretary for the ARMM. In reply thereto, may we respectfully inform His Honor that Asst. Secretary Matalam's powers and authority are clearly defined under Department Order No. 2010-272 dated March 24, 2010, to wit: • In close coordination with other concerned officials, provide the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government (SILG) with advice [assistance in the development and implementation Of policies, strategic plans and programs on peace and progress for Mindanao; Provide assistance to the SILG, through the Undersecretary for Peace and Order, in the latter's capacity as member Of GRP Peace Panel; and Perform other tasks that may be assigned by the SILG. Along this line, we are of the conclusion that, His Honor's query was impelled by the apparent recognition made by Asst. Secretary Matalam in favor of Buldon, Maguindanao Vice Mayor Amir P. Gafor, as the lawful chief executive of the said municipality in view of the alleged physical incapacity of incumbent Mayor Fatima Ruth Tomawis due to health reasons. In this regard, it bears to stress that neither Department Order No. 2010- 272 dated March 24, 2010, the Local Government Code of ARMM, nor the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), empower any agency or official Qt the government to declare a permanent or temporary vacancy in an elective position due to the illness of the incumbent so as to give way to the application of the rule on succession. Let it be noted that due to lack of provision in the two Local Government Codes, it is our consistent opinion that the determination as to whether or not

-2- there is permanent or temporary vacancy due to the illness of the incumbent would necessarily become an adjudicatory matter, meaning, such declaration should be obtained from our courts of justice in order for the said court to adjudicate and apply the law involved. Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUST EA. PANADERO Undersecretary Legal/17
